data.narrative:
GITAI, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $129M+, was valued using a two-method triangulation against a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company in the sector.

The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $129M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $219M. The Peer-Median method benchmarks GITAI against seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—which yield a median valuation of $1.65B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The wider peer set includes Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics, Divergent, and Locus Robotics, as well as public comparable 277810.KQ.

The triangulated analysis produces a median valuation of $935M, bounded by a low of $186M and a high of $1.9B. The substantial variance between methods reflects stage positioning uncertainty: the Stage-Progression result anchors to capital deployed, while the Peer-Median approach captures market valuations at adjacent stages. Key uncertainties center on the appropriate peer discount for Series C timing relative to Series B/D comparables and revenue maturity relative to the peer cohort.
